Monotonic stack

A stack whose values only go one way, top to bottom, answers "who is the first bigger (or smaller) element to my right or left?" for every element in one O(n) pass. That one question hides inside next greater element, daily temperatures, the largest rectangle in a histogram, the maximal rectangle in a 0/1 matrix, sum of subarray minimums, and the greedy "smallest number after deleting k digits". This page builds the four flavours, the pop-time versus push-time rule, the contribution technique with its tie-breaking trap, and the greedy stack, with steppers and tested templates in Go, C++, Java and Python.
